title: Charles IX to Philibert du Croc, undated (1565–1567 or 1572), DECODE R2789

documents.shelfmark: Archives départementales de la Nièvre, fonds du Bourg de Bozas (exact cote not given by Destray)

plaintext.source: George Lasry's plaintext overlay, published by Satoshi Tomokiyo on Cryptiana on 25 May 2022

transcription.source: Lasry overlay checked against authenticated DECODE scans and Destray's Gallica facsimile
transcription.notes: The published overlay leaves several groups as question marks; READING.md preserves those gaps. No independent sign-by-sign ciphertext transcription was made.

system.summary: A sixteenth-century French homophonic symbol substitution with special signs for common words, names, and titles.
system.sibling_key: Lasry's published key for this Charles IX–du Croc system; the 27 April 1567 Catherine de Médicis–du Croc letter uses a different symbol set.
system.notes: The classification and word-sign values come from Lasry's published overlay/key, not a key reconstructed in this project.

prior_solution.where: Satoshi Tomokiyo, Cryptiana, GL.htm, overlay supplied by George Lasry

conditions.human_role: The user logged in to DECODE, making the authenticated images available in the in-app browser.

solution.what: Opened DECODE R2789 with the user's authenticated session and exported both manuscript pages.
Read Destray's cited edition and found the same facsimile on Gallica; it identifies the item as document XLIII, without place or date.
Followed the cited Cryptiana prior art and found George Lasry's complete-page plaintext overlays published in 2022.
Compared the DECODE scans, Destray's Gallica facsimile, and Lasry's overlays; page layout, signatures, and every visible line correspond.
Transcribed the published overlay diplomatically and normalized its secure substance, retaining all visible gaps and uncertain phrases.

outcome.method_basis: George Lasry's plaintext overlays of both pages were on Tomokiyo's cryptiana GL.htm (25 May 2022) before the attempt; the work compared them with the DECODE R2789 scans and Destray's 1924 facsimile and transcribed the overlay.
outcome.notes: The prior solution reads the letter in substance but leaves several signs or short phrases unresolved. No new cryptanalytic solve is claimed.
